primary.thesis: Stealth models with an 'Alpha' suffix on OpenRouter are usually previews that a big lab confirms within weeks, when the production model ships. Quasar/Optimus Alpha became GPT-4.1, Horizon Alpha was an OpenAI GPT-5-era model, and Polaris Alpha became GPT-5.1. OpenRouter usually reveals the developer on its site or X account at launch, which is a qualifying announcement under these rules. 'Ox Alpha' is described as a reasoning model, which fits the pattern of US frontier labs (OpenAI first, xAI second) running pre-launch tests on OpenRouter. Chinese labs have also used the channel recently: Zhipu used 'Pony Alpha' before GLM-5. So the likeliest resolution is an official reveal by OpenAI, with xAI or Zhipu as the next candidates, well before Dec 31, 2026.

basket.reason: OpenAI has the strongest record of 'X Alpha' stealth launches on OpenRouter that are later officially attributed. A late-August reasoning-model preview fits its release cadence.
xAI has used OpenRouter stealth names (Sonoma, Sherlock) for Grok variants. The 'x' in 'Ox' is a weak naming hint, and xAI confirms quickly at launch.
Zhipu (Z.ai) used the animal-themed 'Pony Alpha' before GLM-5. An animal-named 'Alpha' reasoning model points to the same playbook, and Zhipu confirmed that one openly.

failure_narrative: The basket loses in two ways. First, the model comes from a lab outside the basket, such as DeepSeek, Moonshot (Kimi), MiniMax, Alibaba (Qwen), Mistral or Amazon. Chinese labs have been running more pre-release tests on OpenRouter, and a Chinese developer could plausibly pick a zodiac animal name like 'Ox'. Second, the model is quietly withdrawn and never officially attributed. Community fingerprinting through tokenizer quirks or self-identification does not count under the rules, so the market would default to 'Other'.
hedge_thesis: In the worlds where the basket fails, the developer is most likely a Chinese open-weight lab other than Zhipu (DeepSeek, Moonshot, MiniMax, Qwen), shipping a new flagship reasoning model in the second half of 2026. The same competitive dynamic shows up elsewhere. Chinese labs racing to ship reasoning models before rivals is what pushes them into anonymous OpenRouter testing, and it also produces visible events: Hong Kong-listed AI stocks (MiniMax, Zhipu and Alibaba shares) moving on model launches, and Chinese open-weight models climbing benchmark leaderboards. The mechanism: if Ox Alpha is not a US frontier or Zhipu preview, it is probably another Chinese lab's pre-launch test, and those same launches drive Chinese AI equities and Chinese labs' leaderboard standings.
